summary: Dependency-confusion package exfiltrates host identification on install via lifecycle hooks
details: Package publishes to the scope @myorder-frontend-commons and declares preinstall, install, and postinstall lifecycle scripts that all run `node poc.js`. poc.js collects host identification (os.hostname(), os.userInfo(), os.platform(), os.arch(), os.release(), cwd, node version, package version, lifecycle trigger, and the names of CI-related environment variables) and sends it via HTTP GET to two hardcoded out-of-band collectors (db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun and 80-190-83-27.nip.io:80). A hex-encoded `hostname|user|version` string is prefixed as a DNS label to the primary host so DNS resolution alone leaks installer identity. The package.json description self-labels this as an authorized dependency-confusion test against a previously unclaimed scope, but the code path executes on every install regardless of who resolves the scope, exfiltrating installer identity to third-party infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
